title: A DNA-fiber protocol for single molecule analysis of telomere (SMAT) length and extension events in cancer cells
protocol: Add 1:1,000 dilution of 10 mM EdU stock to the culture media for a final concentration of 10 μM.
Gently agitate the flask to mix thoroughly.
Return the flask to the 37°C incubator for 1–5 h depending on cell cycle duration and analysis window.
Melt an aliquot of LMP agarose at 68°C in a water bath for 20–30 min.
Transfer the molten LMP agarose to a 50°C water bath to hold it in a molten state.
Trypsinize or scrape cells for harvesting.
Pellet the cells at 300 g and room temperature (RT) for 5 min in a 15 mL falcon tube.
Resuspend cells in 10 mL of PBS.
Count cell number using a hemocytometer or an automated cell/particle counter.
Distribute sufficient cells in fresh falcon tubes such that 1–2 × 106 cells are allocated to each plug.
Pellet the cells at 300 g and room temperature for 5 minutes.
Aspirate PBS from each sample, leaving behind approximately 45 μL of PBS in each tube.
Immediately place the cell pellet on ice in the dark for up to 30 minutes.
Resuspend cell pellets using a P200 pipette on ice.
Warm the samples quickly in a 50°C water bath for 10 seconds (5 seconds for mitotic cells).
Add approximately 45 μL of molten 1.2% LMP agarose to each sample.
Pipette to mix the cell suspension and agarose.
Immediately pipette each ∼90 μL cell and agarose mixture into a plug mold.
Add 275 μL of ESP solution to a fresh 15 mL falcon tube for each sample/plug.
For each plug, add in the following order: 200 μL of 0.5 M EDTA pH 8.0, then 25 μL of 10% sarcosyl/0.5 M EDTA, followed by 50 μL of 20 mg/mL Proteinase K.
Mix and centrifuge for 1 min at 300 g after each addition.
Push agarose plugs into each falcon tube containing ESP solution using round-headed tweezers.
Flick the tube gently to ensure all plugs are immersed in ESP solution.
Incubate tubes in a 50°C water bath without agitation and in the dark for 16 hours.
Check that the plugs are intact after incubation.
Discard ESP buffer carefully, ensuring the plug remains inside the tube.
Wash plugs three times with TE buffer for 1 hour each at 20°C–25°C while rotating slowly on an orbital shaker wrapped in aluminum foil.
Use mesh gauze to prevent plugs from falling out when discarding TE wash.
Examine each tube during TE wash for the presence of the agarose plug.
Gently tap off any plugs stuck on the gauze using the rim of the falcon tube.
Use fresh TE buffer to wash plugs off the gauze and back into the tube if necessary.
Incubate with rotation for 1 h at 20°C–25°C during each TE wash.
Repeat TE buffer washes two more times under similar conditions.
Wash for a fourth time with TE buffer for 3–4 h.
Discard the final wash after completion.
Store plugs in TE buffer in the dark in a 4°C cold room if pausing.
Set a heat block to 68°C for melting agarose plugs.
Add 1 mL of 0.5 M MES pH 5.5 solution to fresh 2 mL microtubes.
Gently transfer each plug from the falcon tube to the MES solution in the microtube.
Incubate at 68°C for 20 min with aluminum foil covering.
Adjust heat block temperature to 42°C and allow it to equilibrate for 10 min.
Aliquot Agarase such that you have enough for 2 μL per sample plus 20% extra.
Warm the aliquoted Agarase for approximately 10 s on the heat block after 10 min of temperature adjustment.
Add 2 μL of Agarase to each sample and gently invert the microtube to mix.
Incubate on the heat block at 42°C for 16 hours (covered with aluminum foil).
Add 700 μL of MES buffer to fresh disposable reservoirs.
Remove Agarase-digested samples from the 42°C heating block and allow to cool to 20°C–25°C.
Transfer Agarase-digested DNA fiber solution to disposable reservoirs by tipping.
Gently invert the disposable reservoirs to homogenize the DNA fiber solution.
Place the reservoirs in the reservoir bench holder.
Stretch the DNA fibers onto coverslips using the FiberComb® machine.
Bake coverslips at 60°C in a fan-forced oven for DNA-fiber quality check.
Stretch DNA fibers from one reservoir onto an extra coverslip and bake for 1–2 h.
Bake coverslips for 3–4 h for Telomere FISH probing, Click-iT EdU-labeling and YOYO-1 staining.
Let coverslips cool to 20°C–25°C protected from light.
Stain stretched DNA with YOYO-1 to check the quality and density of fibers after Proteinase K treatment and Agarase digestion of plugs.
Dilute the 1 mM YOYO-1 stock 1:4,000 in ABDIL or equivalent blocking solution.
Incubate coverslip with YOYO-1/ABDIL solution for 15 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Remove coverslip and wash twice in 1× PBS for 5 minutes each.
Rinse with deionized water to remove salt traces from your coverslips.
Air dry coverslips.
Visualize on the microscope.
Incubate DNA fibers stretched onto coverslips with TelG-TAMRA PNA probe for non-denaturing FISH.
Wash slides according to protocol steps.
Label incorporated EdU and detect DNA fibers with YOYO-1 in a single step.
Mount stained slides with antifade solution for microscopy imaging.
Subject coverslips to an ice-cold ethanol dehydration series: 70% ethanol for 3 minutes, 90% ethanol for 2 minutes, 100% ethanol for 2 minutes.
Replace ethanol solution according to the ethanol series and repeat from previous sub-step.
Air dry coverslips at 37°C for 10 minutes.
Prepare slides in a dark humidifying chamber by adding 50 μL TelG-TAMRA PNA probe to each slide.
Gently place each coverslip on the PNA probe, label side up (or down if desired).
Incubate at 20°C–25°C in the dark humidifying chamber for 3 h at 37°C.
Label the front of the coverslip rack holder to record the order and orientation of coverslips.
Perform non-denaturing FISH using the TelG (TTAGGG)3 PNA probe.
Release bubbles trapped underneath the coverslip by gently moving the coverslip.
Wash coverslips for 5 min in prewarmed 37°C 1× SSC/50% formamide.
Wash twice for 5 min with prewarmed 37°C 2× SSC.
Wash once for 5 min with 2× SSC/0.1% Tween at 20°C–25°C.
Rinse once with deionized water.
Fix coverslips with 4% formaldehyde solution in PBS for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Fix cells with 4% formaldehyde in PBS.
Discard fixative then wash twice for 5 min with PBS.
Prepare a 1:100 dilution of 1 mM YOYO-1 iodide solution in ABDIL.
Store the YOYO-1 solution at -20°C in the dark.
Prepare the Click-It & YOYO-1 staining master mix as listed in materials and equipment.
Add 150 μL of CYMM to each slide then overlay with a coverslip.
Incubate slides for 30 min at 20°C–25°C in a dark humidifying chamber.
Transfer coverslips back to the coverslip rack holder and wash twice with PBS for 5 min each.
Air dry the slides at 37°C for 30 min in a fan-forced oven or for 16 h at 20°C–25°C in the dark.
Mount the coverslips onto microscope slides using Prolong gold antifade.
Allow slides to cure for 30 minutes at 20°C–25°C in the dark.
Store slides in the fridge in a slide folder in the dark.
Remove slides from the fridge and allow to equilibrate to 20°C–25°C for about 10 minutes.
Perform automated imaging of 2,500–3,500 tiles on the Axio Imager Z.2 microscope or any other epifluorescence microscope with semi-automated tiling capability.
Use the Plan-APO 63X/1.40-Oil objective for imaging.
Select FITC, DsRed, and Cy5 excitation and emission filters.
Enable “Tiles” on the ZEN software.
Change settings in “Focus Strategy” to enable adaptive focus imaging method.
Import an example imaging method file into ZEN software from Methods S1.
Check that YOYO-1 is selected as the reference channel for adaptive focusing.
Set up approximately 20–30 support points on the ZEN Blue microscope imaging software.
Set up tiling according to the settings shown in Figure 3B.
Enable stitching to allow analysis of telomere tracts traversing separate tiles.
Verify the support points by manually adjusting the focus until the YOYO-1 DNA fiber staining becomes focused.
Select “Start Experiment” and allow imaging to perform for 12–16 h, depending on tile imaging area.
Supervise the imaging for several tiles to check that the autofocus is working correctly.
Switch to TAMRA as the reference channel if the autofocus does not work.
